weaknesses: The central distinction between knowledge retrieval and reasoning lacks validation. Its slopes cannot establish diminishing returns per unit of model size or different scaling behavior across cognitive categories. The training conclusions exceed the reported evidence. Table 2 provides only aggregate accuracy, although the introduction claims that SFT improves System 1 but fails to improve System 2. Only 362 of 4,427 questions belong to System 2, so aggregate gains cannot establish reasoning improvements. The best CPT/SFT configuration reaches 51.2%, below the 51.5% instruction-tuned reference, while search raises accuracy to 52.4%. These modest differences lack confidence intervals, paired significance tests, and repeated stochastic experiments.

The inference evaluation leaves important confounds unresolved. The uniform 2,048-token output limit may disproportionately truncate reasoning models, yet truncation rates and budget-sensitivity results are absent. Search methods are not compared at matched computational budgets, and beam width changes alongside tree width. The beam-ranking rule and reflection procedure are underspecified; the described majority-vote selection also leaves the distinction between Best-of-N and self-consistency unclear.

The contamination analysis does not justify the claim of minimal leakage. Appendix F reports original-option-order preference around 10%, versus its stated 4% chance reference, without calibrating detection sensitivity or specificity. This heuristic cannot exclude memorization of question content or paraphrases. Direct overlap checks between the benchmark and the authors’ CPT/SFT datasets are also not reported.

Reproducibility and provenance remain incomplete in the provided manuscript. Release links are blank, individual textbook and question-bank sources and their contributions are unspecified, and the answer-extraction procedure is missing despite allowing unrestricted response formats. Important training details are also absent. The proposed dataset license does not document permission to redistribute the underlying source material. These omissions are particularly consequential because the benchmark and associated resources constitute the main contribution.
